route.marker: The word-event formula and notice close before first-person sweeping speech begins at 1:2.
route.rejected_alternative: Merge the title into the sweeping oracle.
route.counterevidence: The notice frames the entire discourse and needs book-level hydration.

route.marker: Repeated sweeping verbs expand through humans and creatures and close with the speech formula before the Judah/Jerusalem narrowing at 1:4.
route.rejected_alternative: Attach 1:1 or divide the creature register.
route.counterevidence: The cutting-off language continues into 1:4, but the geographic narrowing is a stronger seam.

route.marker: The hand against Judah and Jerusalem introduces coordinated cultic allegiance, withdrawal, and failure-to-seek accusations; the hush summons restarts at 1:7.
route.rejected_alternative: Split the coordinated indictment or merge it into the hush tableau.
route.counterevidence: The catalogue moves from named practices to generalized non-seeking.

route.marker: The hush command and near-day declaration develop through prepared sacrifice and punishment; correlated WLC-family views place a samekh after 1:9.
route.rejected_alternative: Isolate 1:7 or merge the entire day complex.
route.counterevidence: Day language continues into the following city movement.

route.marker: The in-that-day city soundscape moves through merchant lament and lamp search to the complacency saying and property reversal; the great-day poem restarts at 1:14.
route.rejected_alternative: Separate the lamp search and saying from their citywide movement.
route.counterevidence: The public soundscape shifts to private search at 1:12.

route.marker: The great-day restart and repeated day register escalate through battle, darkness, distress, blood, fire, and terminal closure; a samekh follows 1:18.
route.counterevidence: The consequences create recoverable internal stanzas.

route.marker: Repeated gathering, before, and seek expressions culminate in possible concealment; the nations rationale begins at 2:4.
route.rejected_alternative: Surface 2:3 as an independent generic exhortation.
route.counterevidence: The terse wording of 2:1 leaves addressee scope difficult.

route.marker: The causal four-city catalogue prepares the coast woe, desolation, and remnant reversal; the samekh after 2:4 remains evidence for a dependent child seam only.
route.rejected_alternative: Make 2:4 autonomous or sever it from 2:5-7.
route.counterevidence: The samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real child seam.

route.marker: First-person hearing, oath, reversal, pride rationale, and the widened worship horizon form one oracle before direct Cush address.
route.rejected_alternative: Detach 2:11 as an isolated horizon saying.
route.counterevidence: Verse 2:11 broadens beyond the named pair.

route.marker: The second-person address and complete sword clause create a recoverable compass-cycle turn before the northward shift.
route.rejected_alternative: Merge it into either adjacent nation oracle.

route.marker: The northward turn, desolation, animal occupation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby response close together; a samekh follows 2:15.
route.rejected_alternative: Split the proud-city taunt from the desolation tableau.
route.counterevidence: The self-speech at 2:15 is a strong internal turn.

route.marker: The city woe, four failures, leadership accusations, and righteous-Yahweh contrast form one movement before the destroyed-nations example.
route.counterevidence: Verse 3:5 changes from indictment to divine contrast.

route.marker: The destroyed-nations example leads to the quoted correction summons and failed response; therefore-wait pivots at 3:8.
route.rejected_alternative: Attach the whole warning backward or isolate its quotation.
route.counterevidence: Pronoun and causal scope may link the passage more tightly backward or forward.

route.marker: Therefore-wait-for-me plus gathering, assembly, indignation, and all-earth fire form a pivot; for-then turns to purification at 3:9.
route.counterevidence: The verse depends on both neighboring movements and requires the 3:8-13 parent.

route.marker: The for-then turn develops purified speech, shared service, and dispersed worshipers through 3:10; in-that-day shifts the address at 3:11.
route.rejected_alternative: Merge 3:9-13 despite the 3:11 temporal and address shift.
route.counterevidence: The causal opening binds this child to the 3:8 pivot.

route.marker: The in-that-day address introduces proud removal and the remaining humble people, whose speech, rest, and safety close before the samekh after 3:13.
route.rejected_alternative: Merge backward across the 3:11 seam or split the remnant outcome.
route.counterevidence: Purification and remnant formation still form one larger 3:8-13 movement.

route.marker: Song imperatives develop through removed judgment, fear-not reassurance, saving presence, and divine rejoicing.
route.rejected_alternative: Detach 3:17 or divide the song at 3:16.
route.counterevidence: The reported reassurance at 3:16 is an internal speech turn.

route.marker: Difficult first-person restoration language continues through rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the closing says-Yahweh formula.
route.rejected_alternative: Detach 3:18 or 3:20 from the closing movement.
route.counterevidence: The syntax and subject scope of 3:18 remain difficult and may attach backward.

source_gaps: No passage-pinned local primary LXX, DSS, Targum, rabbinic, Second-Temple, or ANE evidence was in authorized scope.
OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family views and may evidence coordinates and samekh locations only; they are not independent textual votes.
The terse wording of 2:1 and difficult syntax and subject scope of 3:18 remain unresolved and calibrate confidence without authorizing a preferred translation.
